Nowe Brzesko Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nowe Brzesko, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Nowe Brzesko developed after residential bans lifted in 1862; population grew to 213 by 1897 and 457 (24.8%) by 1921, swelling to 934 during WWII refugee influxes before most were killed in November 1942 by Germans with the assistance of the General Government's Polish Police. This cemetery, established sometime after 1862, was fenced with barbed wire by the early 20th century and included a mortuary; part of the grounds free of tombstones was used as farmland. Following a 1970 local council resolution, the Minister for Communal Economy formally began closure proceedings in January 1971; surviving documentation notes the plot was leased annually to a named local farmer for 400 złoty.
